title: Terminal-object bar evaluation and compatibility of bar conventions
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a small ordinary category $\mathcal J$, a commutative ring $R$, and a covariant functor $H:\mathcal J\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$, let $K_{\mathcal J}(H)$ be the bar complex of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] for the site $\mathcal J^{op}$ with singleton identity coverings. Let $B_{\mathcal J}(H)$ be the first-vertex bar model of [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation]: its degree $-n$ summands are $H(j_0)$ on chains $j_0\to\cdots\to j_n$, with faces numbered from $j_0$. The identically indexed summands of $K_{\mathcal J}(H)$ have faces numbered from $j_n$. Multiplication in degree $-n$ by $\lambda_n=(-1)^{n(n+1)/2}$ defines a chain isomorphism $\sigma_{\mathcal J,H}:K_{\mathcal J}(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{\mathcal J}(H)$, natural in $H$ and in functors of indexing categories; it is the identity in degree zero and commutes with the degree-zero cocone augmentations.
Let $t$ be a terminal object of $\mathcal J$, meaning that each object $j$ has exactly one morphism $!_j:j\to t$. There is a unique chain map $\epsilon_{\mathcal J,t,H}:K_{\mathcal J}(H)\to H(t)[0]$ whose component on a degree-zero generator $(j,x)$ is $H(!_j)(x)$ and whose components in other degrees are zero. This map is a quasi-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism in $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For the functor $i:*\to\mathcal J$ selecting $t$ and the constant coefficient $H(t)$ on the one-object identity category, the bar reindexing map satisfies $\epsilon_{\mathcal J,t,H}K(i,1)=\epsilon_{*,*,H(t)}$. Here $\epsilon_{*,*,H(t)}$ is the canonical constant-alternating-complex augmentation to $H(t)[0]$. For every small category $\mathcal I$ and functor $u:\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$, the composite $\epsilon_{\mathcal J,t,H}K(u,1)$ is precisely the chain map $K_{\mathcal I}(H\circ u)\to H(t)[0]$ with degree-zero formula $(a,x)\mapsto H(!_{u(a)})(x)$ and zero components in all other degrees. These identities hold as chain maps, and remain the same under $\sigma$ after the corresponding bar-convention identifications.

proof.text: Write $C_n=\bigoplus_{j_0\to\cdots\to j_n}H(j_0)$ and let $b_r$ delete $j_r$, applying $H(j_0\to j_1)$ when $r=0$. The two cited bar formulas give $\partial^B_n=\sum_{r=0}^n(-1)^rb_r$ and $\partial^K_n=\sum_{r=0}^n(-1)^{n-r}b_r=(-1)^n\partial^B_n$ for $n\geq1$. Since $\lambda_n=(-1)^n\lambda_{n-1}$, we have $\partial^B_n\lambda_n=\lambda_{n-1}\partial^K_n$. Also $\lambda_n^2=1$, so the degreewise scalar map is a chain isomorphism with the same inverse. Reindexing a chain, or applying a natural coefficient map to its element, is $R$-linear and preserves $n$, hence commutes with this scalar. Finally $\lambda_0=1$, so every degree-zero cocone augmentation is preserved.

Define $\epsilon_0:C_0\to H(t)$ by the specified $R$-linear map on each summand, and put all other components equal to zero. For $f:j_0\to j_1$, the $K$ boundary is $(j_0,x)-(j_1,H(f)x)$. Its image is $H(!_{j_0})x-H(!_{j_1})H(f)x=0$, because terminality gives $!_{j_1}f=!_{j_0}$. This is the only nonzero chain-map condition into $H(t)[0]$. The direct-sum universal property fixes $\epsilon_0$ uniquely; the other components are forced by their zero targets. The inclusion $e:H(t)[0]\to K$ at the degree-zero summand $t$ is a chain map and $\epsilon e=1$, since $!_t=1_t$.

proof.text: Define $s_n:C_n\to C_{n+1}$ for $n\geq0$ by $(j_0\to\cdots\to j_n,x)\mapsto(j_0\to\cdots\to j_n\xrightarrow{!_{j_n}}t,x)$, extending $R$-linearly from the direct sum. Let $k_r$ denote a $K$ face. For $n\geq1$, $k_0s_n=1$ and $k_rs_n=s_{n-1}k_{r-1}$ for $1\leq r\leq n+1$. At $r=1$ the latter equality uses $!_{j_n}f=!_{j_{n-1}}$; at $r=n+1$ both sides apply $H(j_0\to j_1)$; all other cases delete the same internal vertex. Therefore $\partial^K_{n+1}s_n=1+\sum_{r=1}^{n+1}(-1)^rs_{n-1}k_{r-1}=1-s_{n-1}\partial^K_n$. In degree zero the two faces instead give $\partial^K_1s_0(j,x)=(j,x)-(t,H(!_j)x)$, so $\partial^K_1s_0=1-e\epsilon$. Thus these maps exhibit the homotopy $1\simeq e\epsilon$, including the degree-zero endpoint.

proof.text: Here is the cohomology calculation directly. If $n\geq1$ and $z\in C_n$ is a cycle, step 3 gives $z=\partial^K_{n+1}s_nz$, so every negative-degree cohomology group of $K$ vanishes. In degree zero every element $z$ satisfies $z-e\epsilon z=\partial^K_1s_0z$, and $\epsilon$ kills boundaries by step 2. Consequently the induced maps $H^0(K)\to H(t)$ and $y\mapsto[e(y)]$ are inverse. All positive-degree terms vanish. Thus $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the cited definition, and its image in the localization $D(R)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits); elementary cycle/boundary calculation from the displayed contraction.

proof.text: For $u:\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$, the cited reindexing formula sends $(a_0\to\cdots\to a_n,x)$ to $(u(a_0)\to\cdots\to u(a_n),x)$. Composing with $\epsilon$ therefore gives $(a,x)\mapsto H(!_{u(a)})x$ in degree zero, and zero in other degrees, exactly as asserted. Taking $u=i:*\to\mathcal J$ gives $H(!_t)=1_{H(t)}$ in degree zero. On $*$ every face is the identity, so its degree $-n$ differential is $\sum_{r=0}^n(-1)^r$, namely zero for odd $n$ and the identity for even $n>0$; the augmentation has degree-zero component the identity and other components zero. Hence $\epsilon K(i,1)=\epsilon_{*,*,H(t)}$ strictly. Finally, in either of these equations the only component seen by an augmentation is degree zero. Step 1 gives $\sigma_0=1$ and strict commutation with reindexing, so the same equations hold after applying the bar-convention identifications.
